prompt:
Desktop application UI screenshot, 1536x1024 landscape, for "MLV Studio", a scientific tool for measuring line drawings. Visual world: the calibrated psychophysics display. The entire application ground is a uniform mid-grey #7F7F7F like a mean-luminance experiment screen; white stimulus windows are the only bright surfaces; chrome is grey-on-grey with light grey and near-white text in a plain workhorse sans with tabular figures; a thin red fixation cross is the cursor; colour appears ONLY inside stimulus windows and legends as data encoding (orientation coloured with a smooth cyclic map over 0–180°). Real readable English UI text, flat, crisp, production quality, no device frame, no people.
Composition: canvas-dominant workspace. The white stimulus window is large and centred, occupying most of the screen, showing a black-line drawing of a house, tree and fence with the drawing on white and contours coloured by orientation. No side panels: a thin top bar with "MLV Studio", the drawing name "house1 · 512 × 384 px", and a segmented layer switch: Contours · Junctions · Medial axis · Overlay. A small floating grey readout card near the red fixation-cross cursor shows "c17  length 84.2 px  orientation 37.5°  curvature 1.8 °/px". Junction glyphs (small T, L, Y marks) appear at contour meetings. A collapsed library strip of tiny white thumbnails runs along the bottom edge; at the bottom right a compact orientation histogram 0–180° with a cyclic colour legend.
